newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish industry turns more pro-EMU -survey.
newsitem.headline: Finnish industry turns more pro-EMU -survey.

text.p: More than 70 percent of Finnish industrial firms think Finland should be in the first wave of countries joining the third stage of EMU, the Confederation of Finnish Industry and Employers (TT) said on Tuesday.

It said in a statement that a survey last autumn of member companies found 72 percent in favour of Finnish EMU participation, up from slightly more than 40 percent in its survey in the autumn of 1995.
Weighted for net sales, the survey showed just 0.1 percent of Finnish industry thought Finland should not join EMU at all, TT said.

Chemical industry companies were most strongly in favour with 98 percent for Finland joining from the start, and in metal, engineering and electrotechnical production 68 percent said Finland should participate from the start.
In the forest industry, 67 percent of companies voiced support for Finnish EMU entry in the first wave.
Nearly 60 percent of Finnish industrial companies have already started actively to prepare for EMU, TT said.
The government is working towards making sure Finland will meet all criteria to enter the third stage of Europe's Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) among the first in January 1999.
